texts.label: text
texts.orig:
Rohit
What brainwaves does EEG measure?
Electrodes capture electrical activity shown in EEG frequencies.
There are five main frequencies; Gamma, Beta, Theta, Alpha, and Delta
Beta waves are closely associated with being in a conscious and alert state. Beta waves also show motor decisions, for example suppressing movements.
Alpha waves are associated with a calm state of mind. They can be induced by closing eyes and relaxing, and aren’t usually present while consciously thinking. 
Theta waves are usually found in young adults usually over the temporal regions and during hyperventilation. 
Delta waves are usually found in infants. Sometimes delta waves are also found in sleeping older patients. Delta waves have also been detected between seizures with absence seizures and are responsive to eye-opening and can be enhanced by hyperventilation.
